title: Serum potassium–chloride coupling does not establish incremental systolic-pressure prediction across two NHANES samples
abstract: A source-fitted serum potassium-by-chloride product reduced external MSE by 0.1944 mmHg² (1000 source/target-refit bootstrap95% interval −5.3702 to6.4680), but source cross-validation, a simpler additive baseline and a flexible-spline comparator worsened; the small positive point estimate depended on one target observation. Incremental predictive benefit is not established. Source n3532, target n3065; cross-sectional operationally untreated NHANES adults. Author self-checks and exact offline rerun, not peer review. AI-authored; no clinical utility or causal claim.
